violated = (queue_len_norm>1.0) OR (loss_proxy>loss_budget_pct); per_slice_compliant = NOT violated; margin = min(1, 1-raw_queue_len_norm, 1-loss_proxy/budget)

finding_summary: A fully-starved slice (zero PRB grants) produces dl_errors=0, dl_bler=0 (nothing attempted, nothing to fail) -> loss_proxy=0 -> loss_violation false; if dl_mac_buffer_occupation also reads 0, fallback is also 0 -> queue_violation false. Both channels read compliant simultaneously for zero-activity starvation -- confirmed from source formula alone, high confidence

column5: nr_store_dlsch_buffer() queries RLC's real bytes_in_buffer every slot unconditionally (not gated on scheduling success) -- in principle should show real growing backlog for a starved slice, contradicting a naive 'telemetry pipeline broken' explanation

PDCP implements a real discard_timer -- PDUs older than this get dropped, not delivered, before ever reaching RLC's own queue -- a plausible (not live-confirmed this pass) mechanism for why starvation manifests as silent packet loss rather than growing dl_mac_buffer_occupation

finding_summary: N128 campaign resets ceilings to min=0,max=100 and waits 20s before every 2-episode batch -- a second, not-yet-confirmed candidate contributor to why N128's short/reset batches never showed the sustained queueing M8's longer runs did

Compliance metric is radio-insensitive by construction to complete DL starvation (confirmed, formula-level). Reconciliation of why dl_mac_buffer_occupation itself read 0 is plausible (PDCP discard timer) but marked TODO(MEASURE), not live-confirmed. An above-floor re-run should restore real signal (M8's own non-zero readings under the same broken config support this). Recommend proceeding to P1.
